releases.name: OpenCode Vitals 0.2.4
releases.body:
## [0.2.4] - 2026-11-04

A rate is measured from the step's own provider-active time, not from how
quickly the deltas happened to arrive. An independent audit of the first version
of this fix found three ways an absurd rate could still appear; all are closed
here.

### Fixed

- **`tok/s` could print absurd numbers when a provider delivered a reply in one
  chunk, or a few bursty ones.** The denominator was the time between the first
  and last delivery event, so a reply that took seconds could be divided by a few
  milliseconds. A real record showed **117,666.7 tok/s** for 706 tokens whose
  steps took 9.56 seconds — an honest 73.8 tok/s. The rate now uses each step's
  `step.started` → `step.streamed` provider time, falling back to `step.ended`
  only when `step.streamed` is absent. This includes time to first token, covers
  reasoning and tool-call tokens, and keeps tool execution out of the denominator.
- **Delta spans are never a denominator.** A missing `step.started` used to fall
  back to the first-to-last delta gap and could recreate the exact 117,666 tok/s
  record. Delta spans are now diagnostics only (`streamSpanMs`). With incomplete
  step timing the record says `unavailable`; there is no wall-clock fallback to
  turn a mid-turn join into a number.
- **A failed step with no token record is handled honestly.** Beside a successful
  step its provider time is included with zero known tokens, so it can no longer
  make the turn look faster. If the whole turn has no token record, the rate is
  `unavailable` rather than borrowing tokens from a context lookup that cannot be
  tied to the timed step.
- **A response with no honest rate no longer enters the session average.** Its
  tokens still count in turns, steps and tokens, but they are not added to the
  session numerator without a denominator. The same rule applies when seeding
  history.
- **`null` no longer becomes `0` after a restart.** A rate must be a positive
  finite number; an unavailable reading stays a dash. The launcher host applies
  the same rule and only trusts a current metric marker plus an allowed
  `rateSource`.
- **A partial denominator is no rate.** If only some counted steps have timing,
  the record says `unavailable` instead of dividing all tokens by the steps that
  happened to be timed.
- **A retried step is not rated.** Step events carry no attempt id, so an old
  terminal and a new one cannot be told apart. The turn keeps its turns/steps and
  shows `–` rather than pairing one attempt's tokens with another attempt's time.
- **`last1` inherited rates measured the old way.** A snapshot from before this
  change keeps its turns, steps and tokens, but its stored rate and last1 reading
  are dropped rather than averaged into the new measurement.
- Duplicate `step.ended` no longer stretches the denominator, and a duplicate
  `step.started` no longer erases a completed step's tokens.
- A final `session.text.ended` snapshot extends the diagnostic span even when it
  repeats text the deltas already delivered.

### Changed

- `session.step.streamed` is a measured boundary now, not an ignored event.
- `rateSource` is `step-provider`, `step-ended` or `unavailable`. `stream-span`,
  `first-to-last` and `single-message-total` were removed as rate sources.
- Test fixtures grew burst-reply, tool-settlement, partial-timing, tokenless-step,
  plausible-legacy-rate, null-rate and host-legacy regressions.

### Measured

- 535 checks, up from 494.


---

Upgrade: `npx opencode-vitals install`

releases.body:
## [0.2.2] - 2026-11-03

The second number is the reply you just watched, not an average of the last ten.

### Changed

- **The `last10` reading is now `last1`.** It is the streaming rate of the most
  recent completed response, beside the session average. The session average
  still answers "is this session fast"; `last1` answers "how fast was the reply
  that just landed". A response with no honest rate is skipped, so the reading
  stays on the last response that had one.
- Only that latest rate is kept in the session snapshot. A snapshot written by an
  older version seeds it from the last value in its old ten-rate list.
- The README screenshots were updated to show the new label.

### Measured

- 494 checks.


---

Upgrade: `npx opencode-vitals install`

releases.name: OpenCode Vitals 0.2.1
releases.body:
## [0.2.1] - 2026-10-31

### Changed

- The API pin now tracks OpenCode 2.2.5 (`@opencode/plugin` and
  `@opencode/schema`), which is the release this plugin was last verified
  against. Every event the plugin handles still exists in that schema, and the
  full suite passes against it.

### Fixed

- `session.archived` and `session.unarchived` are lifecycle events, not
  measurements. They are named as ignored, so archiving a session no longer
  produces an "unknown event type" warning.

### Measured

- 494 checks, up from 493.


---

Upgrade: `npx opencode-vitals install`

releases.name: OpenCode Vitals 0.2.0
releases.body:
## [0.2.0] - 2026-10-10

Arabic text reads correctly in messages and the prompt box — folded into the same
plugin, the same renderer copy and the same launcher entry as the readout, so it is
one plugin instead of two.

### Added

- **Arabic text direction.** The renderer copy now also carries `arabic.css` and
  `arabic.js` beside the readout:
  - `unicode-bidi: plaintext` and `text-align: start` on message blocks (assistant
    replies, user messages, compaction, retries) and the composer, so each block
    reads and aligns by its own content;
  - `direction: ltr` on code, diffs, paths and shell output, so those are never
    reordered inside an Arabic paragraph;
  - `dir="auto"` on message blocks, so an Arabic block becomes genuinely
    right-to-left and OpenCode's own `:dir(rtl)` rules mirror its layout, while an
    English block beside it stays left-to-right.
- The three injected files (`vitals.js`, `arabic.css`, `arabic.js`) are copied and
  hashed together, so a change to any of them reaches a copy whose app has not
  moved. A copy missing any of them is no longer treated as ready, and a sync
  rebuilds it.

### Measured

- 493 checks, up from 485.


---

Upgrade: `npx opencode-vitals install`

releases.name: OpenCode Vitals 0.1.18
releases.body:
## [0.1.18] - 2026-10-10

The readout comes back by itself when the server it deferred to goes away.

### Fixed

- **The readout could stay dark until the whole service was reloaded.** When the
  plugin's own bind was refused with `EADDRINUSE` it latched "the launcher host
  owns the port" and never tried again — but the host lives only as long as the
  window it opened, so once it exited nothing served, the running window lost the
  page it was loading, and the row vanished. A liveness probe now checks every few
  seconds whether the port actually answers; if it does not, the plugin stops
  trusting the host and takes the port back. The probe waits five seconds rather
  than half a second, because a server that is briefly busy is not a server that
  is gone.
- A refused bind no longer leaves a server object behind that made the plugin
  think it was serving — which is also what kept the probe above from running.
- The launcher host's own readiness probe uses the same five-second patience.

### Measured

- 485 checks, up from 482.


---

Upgrade: `npx opencode-vitals install`
